title: finding — a gating lint rule shipped claiming "0 findings over the corpus" and names an object that fires it; the corpus copy is not the real app
body:
Recording only — unassigned, no claim. Found while running `objectstack-ai/hotcrm` through 17.2.0 → 17.3.0 as a customer-documentation trial (hotcrm#1576, PR hotcrm#1577). Not folded into that card: it is about **how a rule's blast radius is measured**, not about the rule.

## The measurement

`@objectstack/lint` 17.3.0 ships a new **gating** author-time rule for #14747, `security-controlled-by-parent-ambiguous-relation` (author-time rules 41 → 42). Its changelog entry states the rule was measured over the shipped corpus at **"0 findings before and 0 after"**, and names `crm_opportunity_line_item` as one of three `controlled_by_parent` objects checked, asserting each "declares exactly one required `master_detail`".

The real `crm_opportunity_line_item` in `objectstack-ai/hotcrm` — the repository this project publishes as its reference app — declares **two required lookups and no `master_detail`**, and fires the rule:

```
✗ Author-time rules failed (2 issues)
• object "crm_opportunity_line_item": declares sharingModel 'controlled_by_parent' and 2 of its
  fields tie for the master relation: "crm_opportunity" (lookup -> "crm_opportunity"),
  "crm_product" (lookup -> "crm_product"). … which object this one derives its access from is
  decided by FIELD DECLARATION ORDER … and the runtime reports nothing when it does.
  rule: security-controlled-by-parent-ambiguous-relation  at objects[13].fields
```

`os validate` exits 1, and so does `os build`. Two objects, not one.

## What this is and is not

⛔ **This is not a complaint about the rule.** The rule is right and its diagnostic is the single best artefact in that whole upgrade run — it names the rule, the ADR, both candidate fields, which one wins today, and both ways out. The finding was real: the security boundary on those objects was decided by field declaration order, and the runtime reported nothing when it did. It was fixed in hotcrm#1577 by promoting the intended master into the required-`master_detail` tier, which is the rule's own first remedy.

**The finding is that the corpus the blast radius was measured against is not the application it names.** A "0 findings" reading is exactly the reading that says a gating rule is safe to ship without a migration note. Here it was wrong for the repo the entry names, so a gating rule reached a released minor with no upgrade guidance, and the first person to discover the two findings was an upgrader whose `os build` had already stopped working.

## Why it is worth a card rather than a shrug

Three things compound:

1. **"Measured over the corpus" is load-bearing in this repo's review culture** — it is what distinguishes an assessed change from an asserted one. If the corpus can be a stale or divergent copy, the phrase stops carrying that weight everywhere it appears, not only here.
2. **A number nobody can re-derive is not a measurement.** The entry gives a count but not the corpus's identity — no ref, no sha, no path — so a reviewer cannot tell which tree it was taken against, and neither can the next person to change the rule.
3. **The direction of the error is the dangerous one.** 0 findings understates blast radius, which is the reading that skips the migration note.

## Suggested shape (not adjudicated — this is a record)

- A corpus reading cited in a changelog or PR body **names the tree it was taken against** (repo + sha), so it is re-derivable. Which is the same discipline this repo already applies to `git diff` anchors — a moving ref is not an anchor.
- If the corpus is a **vendored copy** of an external app, the gap between it and that app's `main` is itself a measurement worth having, and staleness in it should be visible rather than silent.
- ⚠️ Worth checking whether other rules landed on the same reading. This one was caught only because someone upgraded a real deployment; a rule with the same stale-corpus assurance and no upgrader would still be sitting there.

## Provenance

Every reading above is from the 17.3.0 upgrade run in hotcrm#1577 (final commit `64f03c79`), whose `pnpm verify` is otherwise green: 160 test files, 3401 tests, `author-time rules (42)`. Related from the same run: #15337 (the dev-admin lockout that blocked its browser leg), #15325 (`@objectstack/cli` sealed its subpaths), and #15322 (the documentation defects).
